questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist preceptor is already directly supervising two pharmacy interns on the same shift. The pharmacy manager asks the preceptor to take on a third intern for that shift, noting that the pharmacy is well under its overall support-personnel ratio. How should the preceptor respond?

choices.text: Accept, because the overall support-personnel ratio is the only applicable limit.
Accept, provided the third intern has already completed 1000 internship hours.
Accept, provided the third intern works only on non-dispensing tasks.
Decline, because a preceptor may supervise interns only in a teaching hospital.
Decline, because a preceptor may not directly supervise more than two interns at one time.

questions.stem: During a busy evening shift a Massachusetts pharmacy intern, who is working under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor, is asked to oversee two pharmacy technicians who are filling prescriptions. Which statement best describes what the regulation permits?

choices.text: The intern may not oversee technicians until licensed as a pharmacist.
The intern may oversee technicians only if the preceptor leaves the pharmacy.
The intern may oversee technicians only after 1500 internship hours.
The intern may supervise pharmacy technicians while remaining under direct preceptor supervision.
The intern may oversee technicians only in an institutional pharmacy setting.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is scheduling a shift and wants to work with four support personnel assisting in filling prescriptions. Which staffing combinations satisfy the minimum supervisory ratio? Select all that apply.

choices.text: One certified pharmacy technician, one pharmacy intern and two pharmacy technicians.
Two certified pharmacy technicians and two pharmacy technician trainees.
One pharmacy intern, one pharmacy technician and two pharmacy technician trainees.
Four pharmacy technicians whose licences are all current.
One certified pharmacy technician and three pharmacy technician trainees.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is working with three support personnel who satisfy the applicable supervisory ratio. A cashier who rings up front-store sales and never assists with prescriptions is also on duty. The Manager of Record asks whether the cashier pushes the pharmacist over the ratio. What is the correct analysis?

choices.text: The cashier is excluded from the ratio because they do not support the pharmacist in a professional capacity.
The cashier counts as a fourth support person and the ratio is exceeded.
The cashier counts unless the pharmacy documents a written exemption.
The cashier counts only during hours when the pharmacy department is open.
The cashier counts as half of a support person for ratio purposes.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy learns that a certified pharmacy technician's certification from the certifying body lapsed last week. The individual's Board pharmacy technician licence remains current. Which consequences follow? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The individual is limited to the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician.
The individual must use the title pharmacy technician.
The individual is counted as a pharmacy technician when calculating supervisory ratios.
The individual may no longer work in the pharmacy in any capacity.
The individual's Board pharmacy technician licence is automatically suspended.

questions.stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy to supply the directions that were omitted from a written prescription already on file. A certified pharmacy technician takes the call after identifying herself as a certified pharmacy technician. What does the regulation permit?

choices.text: She may take the omitted directions only if the prescription is for a Schedule VI drug.
She may take the omitted directions only if she also performs the final verification.
She may not take the information because omitted directions require professional judgment.
She may take the omitted directions with the approval of the pharmacist on duty.
She may take the omitted directions without any pharmacist involvement.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts certified pharmacy technician asks whether he may handle prescription transfers to another pharmacy. The pharmacist on duty is willing to approve. Which transfers may he perform?

choices.text: Transfers of any prescription, because the pharmacist has approved.
Transfers of Schedules III through VI only.
Transfers of Schedule VI controlled substances only.
No transfers, because transfers always require a pharmacist.
Transfers of any non-controlled prescription and Schedule V.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician telephones a prescriber's office for refill authorization. The office authorizes the refill but also increases the daily dose. The pharmacist on duty had approved the technician making refill calls. What should happen next?

choices.text: The technician may accept the change because the pharmacist pre-approved the call.
The technician may accept the change if she reads it back to the prescriber's agent.
The technician may accept the change and flag it for the pharmacist's final verification.
The technician may accept the change only if she is a certified pharmacy technician.
The technician may not accept the change because information has changed from the previous prescription.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee working under the direct supervision of a pharmacist is asked to answer the pharmacy telephone during a staffing crunch and take a new prescription from a prescriber's agent. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The trainee may take the prescription while under direct supervision.
The trainee may take the prescription if the pharmacist listens on a second handset.
The trainee may take the prescription if it is for a Schedule VI drug.
The trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.
The trainee may take the prescription after 500 hours of trainee employment.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee has now worked 1520 hours over ten months. Which statements correctly describe the trainee employment limit? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The limit is 1500 hours or one year, whichever period is shorter.
The Board may grant an extension beyond the limit.
The limit does not yet apply if the individual has not reached 18 years of age.
The limit is suspended whenever the employing pharmacy is short staffed.
An individual who exceeded the limit before turning 18 must apply for a technician licence within 30 days of the 18th birthday.

questions.stem: An applicant for a Massachusetts pharmacy technician licence is 19, holds a high school diploma, is of good moral character and has no drug-related felony. Which of the following, standing alone, satisfies the remaining eligibility requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Certification conferred by a Board-approved certifying body.
A substantially equivalent pharmacy technician licence in good standing in another state.
A Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved assessment examination taken after completing a Board-approved training program.
Twelve months of employment as a pharmacy cashier in a licensed pharmacy.
A letter from the employing Manager of Record attesting to the applicant's competence.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician realises that her licence expired on her birthdate three weeks ago and that she has worked six shifts since. She intends to renew immediately and pay all back and late fees. How should the Manager of Record characterise the six shifts?

choices.text: Compliant, because renewal with back and late fees cures the gap retroactively.
Compliant, because a technician licence carries a 30-day grace period.
Compliant, provided a pharmacist directly supervised each shift.
Non-compliant, but only if the Board opens an investigation.
Non-compliant, because practice after the expiration date constitutes unlicensed practice.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is deciding which support personnel may assist with Schedule II controlled substances during a delivery to a satellite site. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Accountability for and security of Schedule II controlled substances is the direct responsibility of the pharmacist.
A pharmacy technician may assist in transporting Schedule II controlled substances under pharmacist supervision.
A certified pharmacy technician may assist in transporting and handling Schedule II controlled substances under pharmacist supervision.
Written pharmacy policies and procedures must evidence the pharmacist's approval of the individual.
A pharmacy technician trainee may handle non-abuse-deterrent hydrocodone-only extended release medication if supervised.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern withdraws from her PharmD program at the end of a semester. She plans to reapply next year and continues working shifts at the pharmacy. What does the regulation require of her?

choices.text: Nothing, because her intern licence remains valid until its expiration date.
Written notification to the Board within 14 days of the withdrawal.
Written notification to the Board within 30 days of the withdrawal.
Notification by her preceptor rather than by her.
Notification only if she does not reapply within one year.

questions.stem: A PharmD graduate of an ACPE-accredited school has accepted a pharmacy residency at a Massachusetts hospital and will begin next month. She has not yet passed NAPLEX or MPJE. Which arrangement satisfies the regulation?

choices.text: She may practise on the strength of her residency appointment and PharmD degree.
She may practise unsupervised because a residency is a Board-approved training program.
She may practise only after obtaining a Massachusetts pharmacist licence.
She must hold a Massachusetts pharmacy intern licence and be supervised by a pharmacist.
She must hold an out-of-state licence recognised for reciprocity.

questions.stem: A graduate of a non-approved foreign school of pharmacy wants to begin a Massachusetts pharmacy internship next month. He holds NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE that was issued twenty months ago. What does the regulation require before the internship may commence?

choices.text: Nothing further, because an FPGEE authorization does not expire once issued.
FPGEC certification from NABP, which replaces the internship requirement.
A current authorization issued within the preceding year, provided to the Board.
A passing MPJE score achieved before the internship may start.
A letter from the assigned preceptor confirming the supervision arrangements.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts preceptor is reviewing a candidate's internship record against the Board-approved internship requirement. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: One pathway requires at least 1500 hours, of which at least 1000 are in a Board-approved pharmacy or pharmacy-related setting.
On that pathway at least 500 hours must be in clinical pharmacy, a demonstration project, manufacturing, or analytical or industrial pharmacy.
An alternative pathway is at least 1500 intern hours acquired through experiential pharmacy education for a graduate of an ACPE-accredited institution.
The Board may grant credit for out-of-state internship experience on appropriate documentation.
All 1500 hours must be acquired within a single calendar year.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy has just learned that a staff member's technician certification lapsed. The staff member continues to wear a name tag reading Certified Pharmacy Technician while the pharmacy sorts out the paperwork. What should the pharmacy do about the name tag?

choices.text: Change the tag to read Pharmacy Technician.
Leave the tag unchanged until the certification is restored.
Remove the name tag entirely until the certification is restored.
Change the tag to read Pharmacy Technician Trainee.
Leave the tag unchanged if the pharmacist on duty documents the lapse.

questions.stem: A Board inspector asks a Massachusetts Manager of Record for written descriptions of the duties delegated to the pharmacy's technicians and their scopes of responsibility. The Manager of Record has never filed such documents with the Board. What is the correct position?

choices.text: The documents were required to be filed with the Board in advance and the omission is a violation.
No such documents are required in a retail setting.
The documents are required only for certified pharmacy technicians.
The documents must be made available to the Board on request, so they must be produced now.
The documents are required only if the pharmacy uses on-the-job training.

questions.stem: Two applicants seek Massachusetts pharmacist licensure by examination. One graduated from an ACPE-accredited school; the other graduated from a non-approved foreign school. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both applicants must have completed a pharmacy internship in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01(1).
The foreign graduate must have received official FPGEC certification from NABP.
Both applicants must be 18 years of age or older by the scheduled examination date.
FPGEC certification relieves the foreign graduate of the internship requirement.
The ACPE-accredited graduate is exempt from the good moral character requirement.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts applicant passed NAPLEX but failed MPJE. Fourteen months after the original MPJE administration date she applies to retake MPJE. What is the consequence of the delay?

choices.text: Her NAPLEX score is unaffected because NAPLEX and MPJE are scored independently.
She may retake MPJE once more before any additional requirement applies.
She must obtain a Board waiver before retaking MPJE.
She must apply to retake both NAPLEX and MPJE.
She must complete additional internship hours before retaking MPJE.

questions.stem: An applicant for Massachusetts licensure by reciprocity is notified by NABP that she does not meet the requirements for licence transfer. She believes NABP misread her disciplinary history. What avenue does the regulation give her?

choices.text: She may appeal to NABP only, because NABP administers the transfer program.
She may reapply after one year with corrected documentation.
She must instead apply for licensure by examination.
She may request in writing that the Board review the basis of NABP's decision.
She may request a hearing before the Division of Administrative Law Appeals.

questions.stem: A pharmacist licensed by examination in another state seeks Massachusetts licensure by reciprocity. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The applicant must be in good standing in all states where the applicant holds a licence.
A passing MPJE score of at least 75% is required.
Documentation of internship experience in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01 is required.
The applicant may be required to appear personally before the Board.
Reciprocity waives the MPJE because the applicant already passed a jurisprudence examination elsewhere.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is considering petitioning for retired licence status. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Retired status is a nondisciplinary status.
A licensee with retired status may not practise.
Eligibility requires that the licence is not surrendered, suspended or revoked at the time of the petition.
Retired status prevents the Board from taking disciplinary action against the licensee.
The Board must review any later petition to return the licence to current status.

questions.stem: A pharmacist applying to renew a Massachusetts registration discloses an out-of-state disciplinary sanction imposed solely for dispensing medication for gender-affirming health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice here. How should the renewal be treated?

choices.text: Renewal must be denied because any out-of-state discipline is disqualifying.
Renewal may be granted only after the other state vacates its sanction.
Renewal must be deferred pending a Massachusetts investigation of the same conduct.
Renewal may not be denied on the basis of that sanction.
Renewal may be granted only with a probationary condition.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist stopped practising and let his personal registration lapse. It has now been lapsed for about 30 months. It was never suspended or revoked. He wants to return to practice. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: Payment of back and late fees only.
Completion of additional continuing education contact hours only.
Taking and passing both NAPLEX and MPJE.
Taking and passing the MPJE and meeting all other Board conditions.
Application for licensure by reciprocity from another state.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration was suspended for nine months as a disciplinary sanction. The suspension has ended and she seeks renewal. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: She shall take and pass the MPJE as a prerequisite to renewal.
She shall meet all conditions determined by the Board.
The Board may also require her to take and pass the NAPLEX.
Her suspension falls in the band between six months and two years.
Serving the suspension period is by itself sufficient for renewal.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist completed no continuing education in the first calendar year of her two-year renewal cycle. She plans to complete all 40 contact hours in the second calendar year, including 30 hours of home study. Why does this plan fail?

choices.text: Because contact hours may not be earned in the second year of a cycle.
Because home study may not be applied toward the requirement at all.
Because 40 contact hours exceed the annual maximum permitted.
Because a minimum of 20 contact hours is required in each calendar year and hours may not be carried over.
Because pharmacy law hours must be completed before any other subject area.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist oversees sterile compounding in a pharmacy licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, § 39G and also administers vaccines. Which continuing education overlays apply to her? Select all that apply.

choices.text: At least five contact hours per calendar year in sterile compounding.
At least one contact hour on immunizations during the two-year renewal cycle.
At least two contact hours per calendar year in pharmacy law.
At least three contact hours per calendar year in complex non-sterile compounding.
At least ten contact hours per calendar year in sterile compounding because she both oversees and practises in a licensed setting.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist was hospitalised for much of the renewal cycle and completed only part of her required continuing education. She wants to renew. What does the regulation direct her to do?

choices.text: Self-certify the shortfall on the renewal application and renew without further steps.
Renew now and complete the missing contact hours within the following calendar year.
Submit a sworn detailed statement of the extenuating circumstances for the Board to determine.
Apply for retired status until the missing contact hours can be completed.
Request that her employer certify the extenuating circumstances directly to the Board.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist entered active armed forces service in November of an even-numbered year and was released from active duty the following spring. Which statement correctly describes the effect on her registration and continuing education?

choices.text: Her registration lapsed on December 31st of that even-numbered year.
Her registration remains valid until 90 days following release from active duty, and the continuing education requirement does not apply to that biennial cycle.
Her registration remains valid indefinitely while she is on active duty and continuing education is merely deferred.
Her registration remains valid for 90 days but the continuing education requirement still applies to that cycle.
Her registration remains valid only if she requested a waiver before deploying.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is selected for a random continuing education audit. Which elements must her documentation or statements of credit contain? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The name of the authorized provider.
The title and number of the continuing education program.
The date of completion of the program.
The number of contact hours earned.
The registrant's employer at the time of the program.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts provider submitted a program approval request 20 days before the planned presentation date and the Executive Director's designee denied it. The provider wants to challenge the denial. Which statement correctly describes the position?

choices.text: The submission was timely, so the denial can only have been substantive.
The provider may appeal to the full Board by written petition within 30 days of the notice of denial.
The provider must resubmit rather than appeal, because a designee's decision is unreviewable.
The provider may appeal only if it holds current ACPE accreditation.
The provider must appeal within 30 days of the planned presentation date.
